newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean fishermen burn Hashimoto in effigy.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean fishermen burn Hashimoto in effigy.

text.p: South Korean fishermen protesting against Japan's seizure of Korean fishing boats in disputed waters burned Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in effigy on Wednesday in the southern port of Tongyong.
Witnesses said more than 500 fishermen and representatives of civic groups demanded an apology from Japan and asked that two detained South Korean captains be released.
They denounced Japan for capturing five fishing boats in the past several weeks in waters recently claimed by Japan.
"Apologise, Japan, for kidnapping our boats," chanted the protesters, who burned a cloth doll representing Hashimoto and wrapped in the Japanese flag, witnesses said.

"Yesterday it was foolish talk over Tokdo. Today it is kidnapping our fishing boats," shouted the fishermen who were drenched from the pouring rain and headed out to sea to parade their 30 boats in protest.
Tokdo is an outcrop of rock in the Sea of Japan midway between Japan and South Korea and claimed by both countries. The islands are called Tokdo in South Korea and Takeshima in Japan.
Tensions have frequently risen over territorial claims between Japan and South Korea, which have maintained uneasy relations since the end of Japan's 1910-45 colonisation of the Korean peninsula.

Japan, which in January expanded its territorial waters in accordance with a maritime convention introduced by the United Nations in November 1994, has released all five boats and their crew members except the captains of two vessels.
South Korea has agreed to revise a 1965 fisheries agreement but insists the existing pact be respected until a revision is drawn up.
Han Hong-chol, a released sailor, told the protesters that he and his colleagues were badly beaten by Japanese investigators.

Last week, South Korean Vice Foreign Minister Lee Ki-choo called in the Japanese ambassador in Seoul, Shintaro Yamashita, to lodge a formal protest over the seizures and to demand steps to ensure such an incident was not repeated.
